label: Step L+1 (output orig token 1) when the first token q/c/x is fed back, in long sequences
explanation: Fires only at the first copy step after the delimiter (recall_idx == 1, where the input is the fed-back first original token). It never fires in the original phase, at the delimiter, or at any other copy step. About 95% of activations have q, c or x as that first token (q > c > x by rate); y, e and o show up only rarely. Rate goes up steeply with sequence length (none for L<=4, 54% of mass at L=9), and the L>=7 predicate keeps 91% of the mass. It also gets more likely, and in top examples stronger, when j is orig(1) or orig(2) (next_out=j has 18x lift); p, b, z and g in those positions help less. The predicate is necessary but nowhere near sufficient: only about 4% of matching steps actually fire, so the feature looks like a sparse threshold on a conjunction of first-token identity, length and the early original tokens. Adding j at orig(1) or orig(2) raises precision to about 0.3 but halves recall. Magnitude is small (mean 0.13, max 0.25). The highest activations are L=8-9 sequences beginning q/c/x with j near the start.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: recall_idx=1 & in_tok=q (+6.19), recall_idx=1 & in_tok=c (+5.59), recall_idx=1 & in_tok=x (+4.95), orig3=j (+2.97), orig3=b (+2.28), next_out=j (+2.17). Lower it: orig4=r (-2.29), orig7=- (-2.19), orig2=r (-1.95), orig3=d (-1.72).
